additional_info.subject: AW: ID0393072-DC/Si-D/DE[170001715] - ELMS configuration CRM:00315002131
additional_info.body:
Good Morning,
Maybe start at the beginning, with the conditions.
Energu bought and placed a few Siemens Sicharge together with our storage systems at different locations in Germany for their customer.
I phoned yesterday with Michael and he ensured me, that at the location “Autohaus Halbig” the Sicharge with the serial number 170001715 is located. This serial number we are talking about in the subject. The sicharge with the serial number 17001714 should be at “Autohaus Seitz”. Here we have a stable tcp connection. From my point of view not with a normal connection to the wan port of the sicharge router, but instead to the switch. Because we communicate to the sicharge with the address 10.20.17.10 port 400. I explain further below, how I assume we realised the connection.
Back to the subject, “Autohaus Halbig” Sicharge 170001715:
So there is only one sicharge located on side. When the lan cable between the sicharge and our router is connected right (router beck: port 2-5, sicharge router: wan port) and you configured the ip address and port forwarding on your side right, we should be able to get a connection with modbus tcp. That’s the way we tried the 192.168.88.160 with port 400.
As I already mentioned I can’t connect to the TCP port. I’ve also tried another program so that we can exclude, that our sps doesn’t work.
Today I also tested address 192.168.88.161 port 400, still no connection.
To explain why I attempted to connect to 10.20.17.10 and how I think we run the communication in “Autohaus Seitz” serial number 170001514:
Our storage system has an own network, 192.168.88.0 (255.255.255.0), so has your sicharge a network for all your devices inside the charging station. According to the manual this network has the address 10.20.17.0.
On my point of view at the location “Autohaus Seitz” (170001514) the technician on side wired a lan cable from our router (port 2-5) to your
switch
inside the sicharge, see the red line in the attaced picture. We didn’t know any better at this time and it wasn’t obvious from the instruction manual of the sicharge where to connect the lan cable inside the sicharge housing. With this hardwareconfiguration (cable connection) our router is inside of your network directly. We run the tcp connection with connecting our sps directly to your sps with the address 10.20.17.10 (according to the manual). In this case we are skipping your router, where you normally configure the ip address 192.168.88.160 and port 400 (in our network). But since our router is directly connected inside our network, we don’t need this configuration of your router.
Back to the case described inside the manual and also requested by siemens, which we are trying to run at “Autohaus Halbig” 170001715:
We need a LAN connection from (see the green line in my picture):
Beck router port 2-5 to
Siemens router port WAN
You configurated the WAN port with the ip address 192.168.88.160
You configurated a port forwarding of the WAN port port 400 to your sps inside your network (typically to the address 10.20.17.10 and the port which is configurated for the modbus tcp connection inside the program).
My last explanation why the tcp connection is not working is:
We have not the correct LAN connection
We are talking about different locations and sicharges
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Melanie Feser

Mobil:
+49 1515 80329 55
mailto:melanie.feser@beck-automation.de
